messages:
lina (docs): heads up, my tiny PR that only fixes an example snippet hit the 2-review rule and stalled. any lightweight way to let trivial docs PRs auto-merge?
ryan (eng): we chatted about this before. GH doesn't let you set different required-review counts per path. you either change the branch rule or automate approvals.
jess (devex): we've had good luck with a GH App + workflow that: detects docs-only, runs quick checks, posts an approval and a comment, and then labels for auto-merge.
merge-bot: reminder: auto-merge will only proceed once required status checks are green and there are no outstanding review requests.
lina (docs): what are the "quick checks"? link scan + code sample linting?
tyler (infra): exactly. the pipeline should run a link-checker, markdown linter, and a tiny snippet-runner for code blocks. if all pass, the bot approves.
jess (devex): sample workflow we used (simplified):
```
on: pull_request
jobs:
  docs_auto:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: changed files
        run: git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} > files.txt
      - name: detect docs-only
        run: |
          if grep -qE '^docs/|^website/docs/' files.txt; then echo "DOCS_ONLY=true" >> $GITHUB_ENV; fi
      - name: run linkcheck
        if: env.DOCS_ONLY == 'true'
        run: scripts/link-check.sh
      - name: approve
        if: env.DOCS_ONLY == 'true' && success()
        uses: peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v2
        with:
          body: "Docs-only change passed quick checks — posting approval"
```
(Note: approval is done with a bot token that has write permissions.)
lina (docs): thanks. any gotchas with CODEOWNERS? I thought CODEOWNERS could auto-approve.
tyler (infra): CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers, but it doesn't lower the required-review count. so you'd still have N outstanding reviews if branch protection needs 2. automation must post an approval on behalf of a bot account to clear that.
carla (security): small warning: if you let a bot auto-approve, add a rule to exclude sensitive docs: anything under /security/ or /legal/ should still require a human. also keep audit logs of bot approvals.
jess (devex): agreed. we added a deny-list in the workflow:
```
# in workflow
if: contains(github.event.pull_request.changed_files, '/security/') == false
```
and we add a label 'docs-auto-allowed' in the approval comment.
ryan (eng): one more trick — mark the heavier check (docs-build) optional in branch protection and ensure the bot adds a commit status 'docs-build' = success when it ran a minimal verification. that avoids flaky infra blocking merges.
lina (docs): sounds good. can infra draft the action + a one-liner PR template that asks authors to prefix titles with [docs] or add 'docs-only' label? makes detection robust.
tyler (infra): will do. I'll open a draft PR with the workflow, an example CODEOWNERS entry for @redwood-docs, and the PR template. aiming for review by end of week.
merge-bot: note: once workflow is merged, test the flow using a branch to verify bot token scopes and that approvals show in the UI.
